answer.rationale: p99 latency is 5x target during peak settlement traffic. Rollback is blocked by compliance mandate on security patch. Circuit breakers (memory_b4) protect dependent services but don't solve write path saturation. Read replica routing (memory_b5) helps reporting queries, not transactional writes. Regional failover (memory_b2) is viable but introduces cross-region complexity during peak writes. Capacity addition (memory_b3) directly addresses the root cause: settlement traffic at daily peak with insufficient headroom. Memory_b3 shows staged capacity provisioning successfully absorbed retail surge; applying similar approach here targets the write saturation immediately. This preserves the security patch, maintains write fidelity, and gives settlement traffic the resources it needs. Verification of b1 confirms rollback risk if needed; verification of b3 validates capacity strategy during peaks.
